meta.description: George Orwell never wrote it. The line comes from a 2009 column by conservative writer Selwyn Duke — who has spent years reclaiming his own words.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'The further a society drifts from truth, the more it will hate those who speak it'?
meta.ogDescription: Not Orwell. Columnist Selwyn Duke wrote it in a May 2009 article; the internet pinned it on Orwell in the years that followed.

answer.label: Not George Orwell — actually Selwyn Duke
answer.authorDates: American writer & columnist · originated the line in 2009
answer.sourceLine: George Orwell never wrote this. The maxim was coined by conservative columnist Selwyn Duke, who wrote in his essay “Stopping Truth at the Border” (RenewAmerica, 6 May 2009) the words “The further a society drifts from Truth, the more it will hate those who speak it.” Duke has publicly asserted authorship; fact-checkers found no earlier source and confirm it appears in none of Orwell’s works.

source.excerpt: The further a society drifts from Truth, the more it will hate those who speak it.
trail: The line appears in Selwyn Duke’s essay “Stopping Truth at the Border” (RenewAmerica, 6 May 2009) — the earliest known appearance.
Lead Stories confirms Orwell did not write it and found nothing in the University College London George Orwell Archive.
Snopes found no version of the line predating Duke’s 2009 column and concluded Orwell almost certainly did not originate it.
Duke himself later noted his surprise that “Orwell was taking credit for it,” asserting his own authorship.
source.excerptNote: Duke’s original capitalizes “Truth”; the version circulated under Orwell’s name lower-cases it and often inserts “the truth.”
source.rightsNote: The line first appeared in Selwyn Duke’s 2009 RenewAmerica column — a work first published in 2009 and therefore under U.S. copyright. Rights rest with Selwyn Duke (and the column’s publisher). No public-domain claim applies; the Orwell attribution is false.

author.name: Selwyn Duke
author.heading: About Selwyn Duke
author.metaLine: American writer & columnist · originated the line in 2009
author.bio: Selwyn Duke is an American conservative writer and columnist whose work has appeared in outlets such as The New American, American Thinker and RenewAmerica. He coined the “further a society drifts from Truth” aphorism in a 2009 column and has since repeatedly noted, with some exasperation, that it is misattributed to George Orwell.

misattribution.heading: How Orwell got the credit
misattribution.intro: The line is one of the internet’s most persistent fake Orwell quotes. It was written in 2009, decades after Orwell’s death, and mislabeled within a couple of years.

items.why: The sentence appears in none of Orwell’s novels, essays, diaries or letters. Lead Stories found no trace of it in the University College London George Orwell Archive, and Snopes found no version predating Selwyn Duke’s 2009 column.
Duke’s original capitalizes “Truth”; the Orwell-attributed versions lower-case it and frequently add “the” (“drifts from the truth”), as seen against Duke’s source column.

misattribution.truthLine: The real author is columnist Selwyn Duke, who wrote the line in his 6 May 2009 essay “Stopping Truth at the Border” — and has spent years correcting the Orwell myth.

context.heading: Why it sticks to Orwell
lead: The aphorism reads like classic Orwell: terse, moral, aimed at a society that punishes honesty. Because Orwell is shorthand for truth-telling under pressure, the line found a natural — if false — home under his name, spreading across social media and opinion columns in the years after 2009.
The irony is pointed: a sentence about a society drifting from truth became a small case study in exactly that, circulating for years with its true author erased.
context.pull: A quote about drifting from truth, itself detached from its true author.
